newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai Soybean futures ended down in slow trading on Friday on long liquidation by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,298 yuan ($397) per tonne, losing four yuan.
It opened at 3,290 yuan, hitting an intra-day low of 3,288 and a high of 3,299.
July fell two to 3,254, November fell 11 to 3,294, the January 1998 contract fell seven to 3,233.
Combined volume fell to 18,800 tonnes from 19,000.
Soybean opened lower but speculative buying pushed the prices up from lows late in the session, traders said.
"Long liquidation from retail investors dominated today's trading due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
"The sharp rebound on the stock market attracted attention and hot money (speculative funds) from many investors," he added.
Traders said they expected the soybean contracts to move in a narrow range early next week.
